$comment: Written reasons for the capabilities catalogue (docs/DSL_CAPABILITIES.html), batch 9 of N, 2026-11-23 (REG-357, owner: do only 20% of the remaining cases, of mixed complexity). One reason per keyword: what need it serves and why a lower rung of the extension ladder (expression, function, flow step, hand-written code) or an existing keyword cannot do it. The reasons state the need, not the evidence counts: the catalogue's own columns show samples, tests and examples and change as the corpus grows, so a count written here would go stale. The batch is every 5th keyword still without a reason, taken within each kind of value (boolean, text, number, choice, list, object, reference) so simple and complex ones are mixed. Key = slot id exactly as the catalogue shows it; the generator refuses a reason for a keyword the schema does not have.

reasons.packRef.allowSideBySide: An app that imports a pack directly may find that another pack it depends on pulls in the same pack at a different major version, which is normally refused; this flag accepts the two living side by side under a required alias, so an upgrade can move step by step instead of waiting for every dependency to move together.
reasons.guidePageGadget.type: A guide page is a dashboard of different things, such as recent items, context information, a KPI, a bar, line or donut chart, or a table; the type picks which one a gadget is, so one list of gadgets builds the page without a hand-written view for each.
reasons.transactionDerivedField.tier: A derived value in a workbench draft, such as a line total, is cheap to compute in the browser while the person types, but some values, such as a tax that depends on rules, need the server; the tier says where it is evaluated, the browser by default or a named flow over the draft, so the author picks speed or authority per field.
reasons.domainType.examples: A domain type such as an email address or a tax id is easier to understand and to test with sample values; the examples feed the generated help and the tests, so the type documents itself and its tests need no hand-typed fixtures.
reasons.pack:conversions: A pack that changes the shape of its data between versions must bring its data migrations; listing the conversions in the pack, declared in place or from a model file, makes them travel with the pack, so an app that upgrades it gets the rows moved too.
reasons.query.orderBy: A list or a report is expected in a predictable order, such as newest first; the ordered field list with an optional direction, where the first entry sorts first, is declared with the query, so every screen and flow that uses it sees the same order.
reasons.workbenchAction.checkBalances: A person entering an order or a journal wants to know whether the draft balances before saving; naming the balance rules of the aggregate returns a report computed on the current draft without running a flow or saving anything, so the check is a safe on-demand button.
reasons.presentationMetadata.columnSpan: In a form with several columns a notes field needs the full width while a code needs one column; the number of grid columns a field spans sets that shape, so the layout is declared per field and not by custom styling.
reasons.humanTask.proposal: When an AI suggests a change to a record, a person should see what would change before accepting it; the proposal shows the suggested values against the current ones field by field, and the completed event carries them with the record id read from the parked flow state and not from the browser, so a reviewer approves exactly what was shown.
reasons.field.items: A field that holds a list, such as tags or phone numbers, must say what each element is; items gives the element's shape, so the list is checked and stored the same way as any other field.
reasons.workbenchAction.applyTo: An action in a workbench, such as suggesting a line, returns something the person wants as a new row of the draft; applyTo names the collection that receives the procedure's result, so the draft grows without a hand-written script.
reasons.aggregateInvariant.message: When a rule vetoes a save, the person reads its message; the default is built from the rule's name and the evaluator's detail, and this text replaces it with a sentence in the business's own words, so the refusal says what to fix.
reasons.concept.renamedFrom: Renaming a concept without telling the platform looks like dropping a table and creating an unrelated one, which would lose the rows; naming the old concept lets the schema step classify the change as a rename, so existing data follows the new name.
reasons.enumOption.group: A long dropdown, such as a category list, is easier to use when its members sit under headings; the group names the heading a member appears under, so the list is organised in the model and not in a custom control.
reasons.flowStep.collection: A flow that must do the same thing for each line of an order has to say which list it walks; the forEach step names the collection in flow state to iterate, so the loop is declared and its body is plain steps.
reasons.httpConnectorAuth.name: An outside service wants its key in a header such as X-Api-Key or in a query parameter; the name says which one carries it for the header and query key kinds, so the secret value stays in an environment variable and only the carrier's name appears in the model.
reasons.packRef.as: Two packs can offer the same member name, or an app may want a shorter prefix; the alias replaces the pack's own identifier as the namespace prefix in this model, so references read as the author chose and a clash is solved without editing the pack.
reasons.panelSlot.label: A panel that mounts a component, such as a chart, may need a heading so the reader knows what it shows; the optional label appears above the component, so the slot explains itself without a second text element.
reasons.queryComputedColumn.expression: A report column such as margin, revenue minus cost, is derived from other columns of the same row; the arithmetic expression over the output columns, with plus, minus, times, divide, remainder and parentheses, computes it inside the query, so a simple calculation needs no flow and no code.
reasons.transactionHooks.beforeAction: A workbench often needs one guard before any of its actions run, such as the draft being open; the named guard runs first and a result that is not ok stops the action, so the check is declared once for all actions and no single action can skip it.
